body.cap: Aetech’s urban resource circulation station, “multi-tron,” was selected as a CES 2026 Innovation Award winner. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Aetech (CEO Taehyung Park) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

Aetech is a company that has presented automated waste-sorting processes and advanced resource-circulation solutions based on AI vision and robotics technologies. With the goal of addressing structural problems across the waste management industry—such as labor-intensive environments, low sorting efficiency, and quality inconsistencies—through technology, the company develops general-purpose solutions using AI robotics trained on real operational data.

On the strength of these technologies, Aetech has introduced products such as the automated sorting robot “Atron,” the urban resource circulation station “Multi-tron,” and the automated resource recovery facility “Airo-MRF.” Among these, multi-tron earned recognition for its compact AI robotics structure suitable for multi-purpose urban spaces and received a CES 2026 Innovation Award.

At CES 2026, Aetech showcased multi-tron alongside its suite of automated waste-sorting solutions. Atron, which has driven the company’s growth, is a single-robot solution that recognizes waste in real time and performs sorting according to predefined criteria.

Powered by an AI model trained on 5.5 million real-world waste data points and optimized robotic engineering design, Atron sorts up to 96 waste items per minute with an accuracy of 99.3 percent. Following its recognition as Korea’s first commercial AI waste-sorting robot, more than 30 Atron units now operate at public and private sorting facilities nationwide.

Multi-tron features a “dump & go” structure that automatically recognizes and sorts waste deposited by users through an AI system. It delivers strong resource recovery performance even in space-constrained multi-use facilities such as public housing, shopping malls, and stadiums, presenting a model for urban resource circulation. The solution also earns positive evaluations for addressing the limitations of centralized resource circulation infrastructure that traditionally relies on large-scale sorting plants.

Interest also centered on airo-mrf, an automated resource circulation facility built by integrating Aetech’s AI waste sorting technologies. The system improves both operational efficiency and the quality of recovered recyclable materials, enabling the production of high-purity PET flakes. Its modular structure allows the overall infrastructure to be recomposed and reconfigured to suit various site conditions.

Through its participation in CES 2026, Aetech aims to further solidify the foundation for global expansion centered on its automated resource circulation technologies. Based on its commercialization experience and technological competitiveness in domestic waste sorting, the company has progressively demonstrated the global applicability of its solutions. With three consecutive years of participation at CES through this year, it has also collected market needs and feedback over an extended period.

An Aetech official said, “At this year’s exhibition, we presented a clear business message and an integrated solution structure established through our accumulated experience,” adding, “By introducing Aetech’s technological approach that expands from sorting automation to urban resource recovery and decentralized circular infrastructure, we shared the direction of solutions demanded by the global market.”

The official continued, “This exhibition served as an optimal venue to explore future global collaboration opportunities through substantive networking with global buyers, public institutions, and potential partners, allowing in-depth discussions on the application direction and potential of our technologies and business model,” adding, “Building on this CES, we will establish a phased market expansion strategy.”

The Incheon Metropolitan City Government and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority formed the “INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion” at LVCC North Hall during CES 2026, presenting Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as it evolves beyond a smart city into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs, including Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Awards Showcase, the pavilion supported the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES, including 10 companies exhibiting at the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion. In particular, 14 companies won 17 CES Innovation Awards, marking the largest achievement to date and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovative enterprises.
